Pie traces

Source: R/zz-gen-figure.R, R/zz-gen-pie.R
go_pie.Rd

A data visualized by the sectors of the pie is set in `values`. The sector labels are set in `labels`. The sector colors are set in `marker.colors`

Arguments

fig

A go_figure object.

...

Further properties, including nested properties in "magic underscore" form, e.g. marker_size = 10 for marker = list(size = 10). Property values may be one-sided formulas, evaluated in data for add_*() functions.

data

A data frame in which formula properties (e.g. x = ~col, marker_size = ~col) are evaluated. Default: the data given to go_figure(). Only the evaluated values are added to the trace.

automargin

Determines whether outside text labels can push the margins. Logical.

customdata

Assigns extra data each datum. This may be useful when listening to hover, click and selection events. Note that, "scatter" traces also appends customdata items in the markers DOM elements Data array: a vector, factor, Date/POSIXct vector, matrix or list.

direction

Specifies the direction at which succeeding sectors follow one another. One of "clockwise", "counterclockwise".

dlabel

Sets the label step. See `label0` for more info. Number.

domain

Named list or go_pie_domain() object.

hole

Sets the fraction of the radius to cut out of the pie. Use this to make a donut chart. Number in the interval [0, 1].

hoverinfo

Determines what trace information appears on hover. Flags are rendered in a fixed order; use `hovertemplate` if you need explicit control over the rendered string, including the order of fields and surrounding text. Any combination of "label", "text", "value", "percent", "name" joined with "+", or one of "all", "none", "skip", or a vector of these.

hoverlabel

Named list or go_pie_hoverlabel() object.

hovertemplate

Template string used for rendering the information that appear on hover box. Note that this will override `hoverinfo`. Variables are inserted using %{variable}, for example "y: %{y}" as well as %{xother}, {%_xother}, {%_xother_}, {%xother_}. When showing info for several points, "xother" will be added to those with different x positions from the first point. An underscore before or after "(x|y)other" will add a space on that side, only when this field is shown. Numbers are formatted using d3-format's syntax %{variable:d3-format}, for example "Price: %{y:$.2f}". https://github.com/d3/d3-format/tree/v1.4.5#d3-format for details on the formatting syntax. Dates are formatted using d3-time-format's syntax %{variable|d3-time-format}, for example "Day: %{2019-01-01|%A}". https://github.com/d3/d3-time-format/tree/v2.2.3#locale_format for details on the date formatting syntax. Variables that can't be found will be replaced with the specifier. For example, a template of "data: %{x}, %{y}" will result in a value of "data: 1, %{y}" if x is 1 and y is missing. Variables with an undefined value will be replaced with the fallback value. The variables available in `hovertemplate` are the ones emitted as event data described at this link https://plotly.com/javascript/plotlyjs-events/#event-data. Additionally, all attributes that can be specified per-point (the ones that are `arrayOk: true`) are available. Finally, the template string has access to variables `label`, `color`, `value`, `percent` and `text`. Anything contained in tag `<extra>` is displayed in the secondary box, for example `<extra>%{fullData.name}</extra>`. To hide the secondary box completely, use an empty tag `<extra></extra>`. String, or a vector of these.

hovertemplatefallback

Fallback string that's displayed when a variable referenced in a template is missing. If the boolean value 'false' is passed in, the specifier with the missing variable will be displayed. Any value.

hovertext

Sets hover text elements associated with each sector. If a single string, the same string appears for all data points. If an array of string, the items are mapped in order of this trace's sectors. To be seen, trace `hoverinfo` must contain a "text" flag. String, or a vector of these.

ids

Assigns id labels to each datum. These ids for object constancy of data points during animation. Should be an array of strings, not numbers or any other type. Data array: a vector, factor, Date/POSIXct vector, matrix or list.

insidetextfont

Sets the font used for `textinfo` lying inside the sector. Named list or go_pie_insidetextfont() object.

insidetextorientation

Controls the orientation of the text inside chart sectors. When set to "auto", text may be oriented in any direction in order to be as big as possible in the middle of a sector. The "horizontal" option orients text to be parallel with the bottom of the chart, and may make text smaller in order to achieve that goal. The "radial" option orients text along the radius of the sector. The "tangential" option orients text perpendicular to the radius of the sector. One of "horizontal", "radial", "tangential", "auto".

label0

Alternate to `labels`. Builds a numeric set of labels. Use with `dlabel` where `label0` is the starting label and `dlabel` the step. Number.

labels

Sets the sector labels. If `labels` entries are duplicated, we sum associated `values` or simply count occurrences if `values` is not provided. For other array attributes (including color) we use the first non-empty entry among all occurrences of the label. Data array: a vector, factor, Date/POSIXct vector, matrix or list.

legend

Sets the reference to a legend to show the pie slices in. Can be an array if `values` is set. In that case, each entry specifies the legend reference for one slice. References to these legends are "legend", "legend2", "legend3", etc. Settings for these legends are set in the layout, under `layout.legend`, `layout.legend2`, etc. Subplot id: "legend", "legend2", "legend3", ....

legendgroup

Sets the legend group for this trace. Traces and shapes part of the same legend group hide/show at the same time when toggling legend items. String.

legendgrouptitle

Named list or go_pie_legendgrouptitle() object.

legendrank

Sets the legend rank for this pie. If passed as an array, this will set the legend rank of the individual pie slices. Items and groups with smaller ranks are presented on top/left side while with "reversed" `legend.traceorder` they are on bottom/right side. The default legendrank is 1000, so that you can use ranks less than 1000 to place certain items before all unranked items, and ranks greater than 1000 to go after all unranked items. When having unranked or equal rank items shapes would be displayed after traces i.e. according to their order in data and layout. Number, or a vector of these.

legendwidth

Sets the width (in px or fraction) of the legend for this trace. Number in the interval [0, Inf].

marker

Named list or go_pie_marker() object.

meta

Assigns extra meta information associated with this trace that can be used in various text attributes. Attributes such as trace `name`, graph, axis and colorbar `title.text`, annotation `text` `rangeselector`, `updatemenues` and `sliders` `label` text all support `meta`. To access the trace `meta` values in an attribute in the same trace, simply use `%{meta[i]}` where `i` is the index or key of the `meta` item in question. To access trace `meta` in layout attributes, use `%{data[n[.meta[i]}` where `i` is the index or key of the `meta` and `n` is the trace index. Any value.

name

Sets the trace name. The trace name appears as the legend item and on hover. String.

opacity

Sets the opacity of the trace. Number in the interval [0, 1].

outsidetextfont

Sets the font used for `textinfo` lying outside the sector. Named list or go_pie_outsidetextfont() object.

pull

Sets the fraction of larger radius to pull the sectors out from the center. This can be a constant to pull all slices apart from each other equally or an array to highlight one or more slices. Number in the interval [0, 1], or a vector of these.

rotation

Instead of the first slice starting at 12 o'clock, rotate to some other angle. Angle in degrees.

scalegroup

If there are multiple pie charts that should be sized according to their totals, link them by providing a non-empty group id here shared by every trace in the same group. String.

showlegend

Determines whether or not items corresponding to the pie slices are shown in the legend. Can be an array if `values` is set. In that case, each entry specifies appearance in the legend for one slice. Logical, or a vector of these.

sort

Determines whether or not the sectors are reordered from largest to smallest. Logical.

text

go_pie(): Sets text elements associated with each sector. If trace `textinfo` contains a "text" flag, these elements will be seen on the chart. If trace `hoverinfo` contains a "text" flag and "hovertext" is not set, these elements will be seen in the hover labels. Data array: a vector, factor, Date/POSIXct vector, matrix or list.

go_pie_legendgrouptitle(): Sets the title of the legend group. String.

go_pie_title(): Sets the title of the chart. If it is empty, no title is displayed. String.

textfont

Sets the font used for `textinfo`. Named list or go_pie_textfont() object.

textinfo

Determines what trace information appears on the graph. Flags are rendered in a fixed order; use `texttemplate` if you need explicit control over the rendered string, including the order of fields and surrounding text. Any combination of "label", "text", "value", "percent" joined with "+", or one of "none".

textposition

Specifies the location of the `textinfo`. One of "inside", "outside", "auto", "none", or a vector of these.

texttemplate

Template string used for rendering the information text that appears on points. Note that this will override `textinfo`. Variables are inserted using %{variable}, for example "y: %{y}". Numbers are formatted using d3-format's syntax %{variable:d3-format}, for example "Price: %{y:$.2f}". https://github.com/d3/d3-format/tree/v1.4.5#d3-format for details on the formatting syntax. Dates are formatted using d3-time-format's syntax %{variable|d3-time-format}, for example "Day: %{2019-01-01|%A}". https://github.com/d3/d3-time-format/tree/v2.2.3#locale_format for details on the date formatting syntax. Variables that can't be found will be replaced with the specifier. For example, a template of "data: %{x}, %{y}" will result in a value of "data: 1, %{y}" if x is 1 and y is missing. Variables with an undefined value will be replaced with the fallback value. All attributes that can be specified per-point (the ones that are `arrayOk: true`) are available. Finally, the template string has access to variables `label`, `color`, `value`, `percent` and `text`. String, or a vector of these.

texttemplatefallback

Fallback string that's displayed when a variable referenced in a template is missing. If the boolean value 'false' is passed in, the specifier with the missing variable will be displayed. Any value.

title

String (the title text), named list or go_pie_title() object.

uid

Assign an id to this trace, Use this to provide object constancy between traces during animations and transitions. String.

uirevision

Controls persistence of some user-driven changes to the trace: `constraintrange` in `parcoords` traces, as well as some `editable: true` modifications such as `name` and `colorbar.title`. Defaults to `layout.uirevision`. Note that other user-driven trace attribute changes are controlled by `layout` attributes: `trace.visible` is controlled by `layout.legend.uirevision`, `selectedpoints` is controlled by `layout.selectionrevision`, and `colorbar.(x|y)` (accessible with `config: {editable: true}`) is controlled by `layout.editrevision`. Trace changes are tracked by `uid`, which only falls back on trace index if no `uid` is provided. So if your app can add/remove traces before the end of the `data` array, such that the same trace has a different index, you can still preserve user-driven changes if you give each trace a `uid` that stays with it as it moves. Any value.

values

Sets the values of the sectors. If omitted, we count occurrences of each label. Data array: a vector, factor, Date/POSIXct vector, matrix or list.

visible

Determines whether or not this trace is visible. If "legendonly", the trace is not drawn, but can appear as a legend item (provided that the legend itself is visible). One of "legendonly", TRUE, FALSE.

row

add_pie(): Subplot grid row (figures created with make_subplots() only). May be "all" or a vector to address several cells.

go_pie_domain(): If there is a layout grid, use the domain for this row in the grid for this pie trace. Integer in the interval [0, Inf].

col

Subplot grid column (figures created with make_subplots() only). May be "all" or a vector to address several cells.

skip_invalid

If TRUE, silently drop invalid properties instead of raising an error.

arg

Optional named list, or graph object of the same type, to initialise properties from (constructors). Named arguments take precedence.

column

If there is a layout grid, use the domain for this column in the grid for this pie trace. Integer in the interval [0, Inf].

x

Sets the horizontal domain of this pie trace (in plot fraction). Vector or list of 2 element(s).

y

Sets the vertical domain of this pie trace (in plot fraction). Vector or list of 2 element(s).

align

Sets the horizontal alignment of the text content within hover label box. Has an effect only if the hover label text spans two or more lines One of "left", "right", "auto", or a vector of these.

bgcolor

go_pie_hoverlabel(): Sets the background color of the hover labels for this trace Color: a CSS color string or R color name, or a vector of these.

go_pie_marker_pattern(): When there is no colorscale sets the color of background pattern fill. Defaults to a `marker.color` background when `fillmode` is "overlay". Otherwise, defaults to a transparent background. Color: a CSS color string or R color name, or a vector of these.

bordercolor

Sets the border color of the hover labels for this trace. Color: a CSS color string or R color name, or a vector of these.

font

go_pie_hoverlabel(): Sets the font used in hover labels. Named list or go_pie_hoverlabel_font() object.

go_pie_legendgrouptitle(): Sets this legend group's title font. Named list or go_pie_legendgrouptitle_font() object.

go_pie_title(): Sets the font used for `title`. Named list or go_pie_title_font() object.

namelength

Sets the default length (in number of characters) of the trace name in the hover labels for all traces. -1 shows the whole name regardless of length. 0-3 shows the first 0-3 characters, and an integer >3 will show the whole name if it is less than that many characters, but if it is longer, will truncate to `namelength - 3` characters and add an ellipsis. Integer in the interval [-1, Inf], or a vector of these.

showarrow

Sets whether or not to show the hover label arrow/triangle pointing to the data point. Logical.

color

go_pie_hoverlabel_font(), go_pie_insidetextfont(), go_pie_outsidetextfont(), go_pie_textfont(), go_pie_title_font(): Color: a CSS color string or R color name, or a vector of these.

go_pie_legendgrouptitle_font(): Color: a CSS color string or R color name.

go_pie_marker_line(): Sets the color of the line enclosing each sector. Color: a CSS color string or R color name, or a vector of these.

family

go_pie_hoverlabel_font(), go_pie_insidetextfont(), go_pie_outsidetextfont(), go_pie_textfont(), go_pie_title_font(): HTML font family - the typeface that will be applied by the web browser. The web browser can only apply a font if it is available on the system where it runs. Provide multiple font families, separated by commas, to indicate the order in which to apply fonts if they aren't available. String, or a vector of these.

go_pie_legendgrouptitle_font(): HTML font family - the typeface that will be applied by the web browser. The web browser can only apply a font if it is available on the system where it runs. Provide multiple font families, separated by commas, to indicate the order in which to apply fonts if they aren't available. String.

lineposition

go_pie_hoverlabel_font(), go_pie_insidetextfont(), go_pie_outsidetextfont(), go_pie_textfont(), go_pie_title_font(): Sets the kind of decoration line(s) with text, such as an "under", "over" or "through" as well as combinations e.g. "under+over", etc. Any combination of "under", "over", "through" joined with "+", or one of "none", or a vector of these.

go_pie_legendgrouptitle_font(): Sets the kind of decoration line(s) with text, such as an "under", "over" or "through" as well as combinations e.g. "under+over", etc. Any combination of "under", "over", "through" joined with "+", or one of "none".

shadow

go_pie_hoverlabel_font(), go_pie_insidetextfont(), go_pie_outsidetextfont(), go_pie_textfont(), go_pie_title_font(): Sets the shape and color of the shadow behind text. "auto" places minimal shadow and applies contrast text font color. See https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/text-shadow for additional options. String, or a vector of these.

go_pie_legendgrouptitle_font(): Sets the shape and color of the shadow behind text. "auto" places minimal shadow and applies contrast text font color. See https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/text-shadow for additional options. String.

size

go_pie_hoverlabel_font(), go_pie_insidetextfont(), go_pie_outsidetextfont(), go_pie_textfont(), go_pie_title_font(): Number in the interval [1, Inf], or a vector of these.

go_pie_legendgrouptitle_font(): Number in the interval [1, Inf].

go_pie_marker_pattern(): Sets the size of unit squares of the pattern fill in pixels, which corresponds to the interval of repetition of the pattern. Number in the interval [0, Inf], or a vector of these.

style

go_pie_hoverlabel_font(), go_pie_insidetextfont(), go_pie_outsidetextfont(), go_pie_textfont(), go_pie_title_font(): Sets whether a font should be styled with a normal or italic face from its family. One of "normal", "italic", or a vector of these.

go_pie_legendgrouptitle_font(): Sets whether a font should be styled with a normal or italic face from its family. One of "normal", "italic".

textcase

go_pie_hoverlabel_font(), go_pie_insidetextfont(), go_pie_outsidetextfont(), go_pie_textfont(), go_pie_title_font(): Sets capitalization of text. It can be used to make text appear in all-uppercase or all-lowercase, or with each word capitalized. One of "normal", "word caps", "upper", "lower", or a vector of these.

go_pie_legendgrouptitle_font(): Sets capitalization of text. It can be used to make text appear in all-uppercase or all-lowercase, or with each word capitalized. One of "normal", "word caps", "upper", "lower".

variant

go_pie_hoverlabel_font(), go_pie_insidetextfont(), go_pie_outsidetextfont(), go_pie_textfont(), go_pie_title_font(): Sets the variant of the font. One of "normal", "small-caps", "all-small-caps", "all-petite-caps", "petite-caps", "unicase", or a vector of these.

go_pie_legendgrouptitle_font(): Sets the variant of the font. One of "normal", "small-caps", "all-small-caps", "all-petite-caps", "petite-caps", "unicase".

weight

go_pie_hoverlabel_font(), go_pie_insidetextfont(), go_pie_outsidetextfont(), go_pie_textfont(), go_pie_title_font(): Sets the weight (or boldness) of the font. Integer in the interval [1, 1000], or a vector of these.

go_pie_legendgrouptitle_font(): Sets the weight (or boldness) of the font. Integer in the interval [1, 1000].

colors

Sets the color of each sector. If not specified, the default trace color set is used to pick the sector colors. Data array: a vector, factor, Date/POSIXct vector, matrix or list.

line

Named list or go_pie_marker_line() object.

pattern

Sets the pattern within the marker. Named list or go_pie_marker_pattern() object.

width

Sets the width (in px) of the line enclosing each sector. Number in the interval [0, Inf], or a vector of these.

fgcolor

When there is no colorscale sets the color of foreground pattern fill. Defaults to a `marker.color` background when `fillmode` is "replace". Otherwise, defaults to dark grey or white to increase contrast with the `bgcolor`. Color: a CSS color string or R color name, or a vector of these.

fgopacity

Sets the opacity of the foreground pattern fill. Defaults to a 0.5 when `fillmode` is "overlay". Otherwise, defaults to 1. Number in the interval [0, 1].

fillmode

Determines whether `marker.color` should be used as a default to `bgcolor` or a `fgcolor`. One of "replace", "overlay".

path

Sets a custom path for pattern fill. Use with no `shape` or `solidity`, provide an SVG path string for the regions of the square from (0,0) to (`size`,`size`) to color. String, or a vector of these.

shape

Sets the shape of the pattern fill. By default, no pattern is used for filling the area. One of "", "/", "\\", "x", "-", "|", "+", ".", or a vector of these.

solidity

Sets the solidity of the pattern fill. Solidity is roughly the fraction of the area filled by the pattern. Solidity of 0 shows only the background color without pattern and solidty of 1 shows only the foreground color without pattern. Number in the interval [0, 1], or a vector of these.

position

Specifies the location of the `title`. One of "top left", "top center", "top right", "middle center", "bottom left", "bottom center", "bottom right".

Value

Each go_*() function returns a graph object of the same class as its name; add_*() functions return the modified figure.

Details

go_pie() and the nested object constructors below create validated graph objects (named lists). Every property is checked against the plotly.js schema when an object is created or modified (see plotly_obj-modify()). add_pie() creates an object and adds it to a figure.

Nested objects documented here:

go_pie_domain()

pie.domain

go_pie_hoverlabel()

pie.hoverlabel

go_pie_hoverlabel_font()

pie.hoverlabel.font: Sets the font used in hover labels.

go_pie_insidetextfont()

pie.insidetextfont: Sets the font used for `textinfo` lying inside the sector.

go_pie_legendgrouptitle()

pie.legendgrouptitle

go_pie_legendgrouptitle_font()

pie.legendgrouptitle.font: Sets this legend group's title font.

go_pie_marker()

pie.marker

go_pie_marker_line()

pie.marker.line

go_pie_marker_pattern()

pie.marker.pattern: Sets the pattern within the marker.

go_pie_outsidetextfont()

pie.outsidetextfont: Sets the font used for `textinfo` lying outside the sector.

go_pie_textfont()

pie.textfont: Sets the font used for `textinfo`.

go_pie_title()

pie.title

go_pie_title_font()

pie.title.font: Sets the font used for `title`.

See also

go_figure(), add_trace()

Examples

go_pie()
#> <go_pie>
#> {
#>   "type": "pie"
#> }
